note: 20 Oct 2026 - 'The #1 Hack For Overcoming Adversity' (Rumble v6j5tha). Weekly agent.

clips.caption:
Two people hit the same wall. One stares at the problem. The other keeps staring at the goal.

Kevin Trudeau says that's the entire hack for adversity - where you look. Fixate on the problem and, per Earl Nightingale's old rule, you become what you think about most and the problem grows.

Keep your eye on the dream instead, and he says the universe starts working for you, not against you.

It isn't about ignoring the mountain in front of you - it's about which side of it you spend your energy staring at.

Right now, is your attention on the problem or on the goal?

#kevintrudeau #mindsetmatters #adversity #successhabits #lawofattraction #moneymindset

The Federal Trade Commission sued Kevin Trudeau over a coral calcium infomercial, trying to wipe him out financially and shut him down completely.

The settlement banned him from TV infomercials for any product, ending his entire business model overnight.

Reading the fine print, he found one line the FTC's own lawyers signed off on: the ban didn't cover infomercials for books, protected under the First Amendment.

His own team told him it was pointless - nobody had ever made money selling a book on TV.

What's the fine print you haven't actually read in your own biggest setback?

#kevintrudeau #adversity #entrepreneurmindset #successhabits #businesslessons #moneymindset

Banned from selling products on TV, Kevin Trudeau decided to write about the one thing the government had just sued him for talking about - natural health.

After a few tries at the title, he landed on one: a natural-health expose book the government wouldn't want you to read.

His own team said a book would never work as an infomercial. No one had done it. Not enough margin.

It became the number one best-selling book in America that year, 26 weeks atop the New York Times list, and sold almost 50 million copies in hardcover.

What idea have you dismissed just because no one else has done it?

#kevintrudeau #naturalcures #successhabits #adversity #entrepreneurmindset #businesslessons

A few years after his bestselling health book landed him in court again, the government hit Kevin Trudeau with a new judgment: $37 million he didn't have.

He says his legal team laid it out plainly - a receiver would take the houses, the cars, even the toothbrushes. Everything, liquidated.

Sitting with that, he asked one question: what if the next thing he built wasn't his to seize? A brand new foundation, owned by no one, holding nothing he'd ever transferred into it.

Out of that $37 million judgment came the organization he'd wanted to build his entire career.

What would you build if you couldn't lose it to anyone?

#kevintrudeau #adversity #moneymindset #businesslessons #successhabits #entrepreneurmindset

Kevin Trudeau was convicted of contempt of court - not a crime, he says, but still handed the longest sentence in US history for it: 10 years in federal prison.

He thought of Viktor Frankl's line from a Nazi concentration camp - they can take everything except control of your own mind.

With no phone, no email, and years ahead of him, he used the time to write down every lesson, every technique he'd ever learned on paper.

That became the Science of Personal Mastery course - something he says would not exist today without that sentence.

What would you build if you had nothing left to do but build it?

#kevintrudeau #adversity #mindsetmatters #successhabits #prisonstory #moneymindset

Transferred between federal prisons, Kevin Trudeau was stripped, dressed in paper slippers and a paper t-shirt, and marched onto a freezing tarmac at O'Hare in 20-degree weather.

Other inmates shivered and some nearly cried. He says he used breath of fire, the same technique Tibetan monks use to melt snow around their bodies while meditating half-naked in the Himalayas.

A guard noticed he wasn't shaking and asked how. His answer: "You can train your mind to do anything."

No special conditions. No warning. Just a technique and a decision.

What's one thing you've assumed your body just can't handle?
